content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) at § 7.6 (p0032).**

- **Issue:** § 7.6 requires Customer to pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for *any* delay in providing a dependency — an uncapped penalty on us, triggered by a minor breach, with no notice, materiality threshold, or aggregate cap. This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees).
- **Scope check:** No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum termination fee exists in the document (searches for "liquidated" and "termination fee" returned only § 7.6); § 21.2 and § 12.3 raise no LD exposure, and there is no offsetting service-credit regime in the body.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** Replaces the daily LD with a good-faith equitable adjustment to the affected schedule on Vendor notice, and expressly confirms no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by us — preserving Vendor's legitimate schedule relief for delays it did not cause.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") satisfies the preferred TRANSITION position on every material term:

- **11.1** — up to **six months** transition assistance on expiry or termination for any reason, at the expiring Order Form rates, including knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, and continued service at then-current scope and service levels.
- **11.2** — return of all Customer Data within **thirty days** in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with metadata and relationships, and an express prohibition on holding data hostage over a fee dispute (better than model language).
- **11.3** — secure deletion after we confirm successful return, certified in writing by an authorized officer, with any legally required retained copy remaining protected and use-restricted.

Cross-check: Section 16.5 expressly defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, so the confidentiality return/destroy mechanic does not undercut these exit rights, and Section 10.1 preserves access during the agreed transition period. No walk-away features (immediate deletion or no data return) appear anywhere in the document.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement satisfies the MINCOMMIT preferred position:

- **§ 2.1 (p0012)** — expressly states "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," ties fees to Services actually ordered under an executed Order Form, and confirms that declining to place a further order "is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** — bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use, platform, support, or administration charge not identified in the Order Form.
- **§ 12.3 (p0050)** — records that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, or minimum-volume commitment.

No take-or-pay, forecast obligation, or volume cap on our usage exists. The "shortfall" language in §§ 22.2–22.3 is a usage-audit true-up for under-reported consumption — the true-up mechanic the playbook favours — not a penalty. The § 7.6 liquidated damages for dependency delay is a distinct commercial term properly handled under the LD rule, so it is not double-flagged here.

You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer

Preferred position:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.


Fallback position:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
22. AUDIT RIGHTS
22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Rendered redlined clause:
22. AUDIT RIGHTS
22.1 Vendor may audit Customer no more than once in any 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, and may not remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
The audit shall be conducted during business hours, off-site where possible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and at Vendor's cost unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 5% for the audited period.
22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core ri[REDACTED] provisions are in good shape: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), warranties (§ 19), insurance (§ 18), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law and venue (§ 28), and the absence of minimum commitments (§ 2.1) all meet our preferred position, with only minor sub-elements short of ideal wording that we do not propose to redline.

The problems are concentrated in a cluster of Customer-burdening commercial terms that appear to have been inserted inconsistently with the rest of the document: an unlimited, no-notice Vendor audit right with remote system access (§ 22.1), a sole-source exclusivity obligation on us (§ 2.2), a Customer-side most-favoured-nation covenant (§ 7.2), uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by us (§ 7.6), an eighteen-month no-hire (§ 12.4), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), and the complete absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a three-year term with twelve-month auto-renewals. Several of these directly contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, and § 2.1, which disclaims any purchase commitment — so deletion also restores internal consistency.

Six items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook. Redlines have been prepared for each deviation; the § 22.1 audit redline did not pass automated verification and requires manual drafting before it goes out.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems; walk-away. Redline pending manual verification. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Sole and exclusive provider for hosted analytics for the full term; fails fallback; contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended MFN running against us; no product, time or comparison limits; contradicts § 12.3. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day, uncapped, triggered by "any delay in providing a dependency"; fails preferred and fallback. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way, 18 months post-termination, all Vendor employees, and an effective no-hire. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | § 8.2 | 180-day opt-out window exceeds the 60-day fallback; walk-away. Renewal pricing (§ 8.3) is favourable. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9.3 (cause-based rights only) | No Customer convenience right anywhere in a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals; walk-away. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 | Full preferred position; indemnities are Excluded Claims under § 21.3, better than the 3× fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 | Customer ownership of data and Deliverables; minor points on payment condition and sublicensing noted only. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full carve-outs. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free Customer assignment; no change-of-control trigger operates against us. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 | Affiliates and contractors included; § 13.2 perpetual licence for paid-up Vendor Technology. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No field-of-use or competitive restraint; § 2.2 addressed under the exclusivity rule. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 | New York law, New York County courts, no arbitration; mutual escalation and injunctive carve-out. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 | No minimum, take-or-pay or forecast obligation; §§ 22.2–22.3 are true-ups, not penalties. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 | Six months' assistance at Order Form rates; 30-day data return; no fee-dispute withholding. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Services warranty for the subscription term; mutual, non-swallowing disclaimer in § 19.5. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | All required limits met; insurance expressly does not limit Vendor's liabilities. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit rights.** Audits at any time, without notice, with remote access to our systems. No frequency limit, no notice, direct system access.
2. **§ 2.2 — Sole-source exclusivity.** Full-term sole and exclusive provider obligation with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no performance-based exit.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended, with no defined product or service, no time limit and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
4. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away.
5. **Termination for convenience — absent.** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term with auto-renewals.
6. **§ 7.6 — Liquidated damages.** Uncapped daily accrual for minor breaches approaches walk-away territory.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the prepared redlines** on §§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6, 8.2 and 12.4, and insert a new § 9.4 (Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, consistent with the refund mechanic in § 10.2, and confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right).
